title: Descriptive Catalogue of the Loan Collection of Pictures
subtitle: Prepared by the authority of the Library Committee of the Corporation of the City of London
venue: Art Gallery of the Corporation of London (Guildhall Art Gallery)
organiser: Library Committee of the Corporation of London; catalogued by A. G. Temple
label: Guildhall 1892
notes: The scan of this catalogue is rough, and its ‘Lent by’ lines are the worst-read part of it: 167 of the 180 lenders have been supplied from the catalogue’s own Index of Contributors, each flagged in its record’s note; two lenders could not be recovered at all. Ten catalogue numbers were illegible and restored from their sequence position, each flagged; one title (no. 171) is lost from the scan. Graves’s Century of Loan Exhibitions digests this exhibition but covers only 154 of its 180 works — the printed catalogue is the authority here. Names and titles are as printed and carry the scan’s OCR noise. No images in this first version.

title: Descriptive Catalogue of the Loan Collection of Pictures
subtitle: Prepared by A. G. Temple, F.S.A., Director of the Art Gallery of the Corporation of London
venue: Art Gallery of the Corporation of London (Guildhall Art Gallery)
label: Guildhall 1894
notes: Thirty-nine catalogue numbers were illegible or garbled in the scan and have been restored from their sequence position, each flagged in its record’s note; two lenders were supplied from the catalogue’s own Index of Contributors, each flagged, and two could not be recovered at all. Three sizes are lost from damaged scan lines and one title (no. 125) is absent from the scan. Names and titles keep the scan’s reading, garbles included. Graves’s Century of Loan Exhibitions digests this exhibition but covers only 143 of its 154 works — the printed catalogue is the authority here.

title: Catalogue of the Loan Collection of Pictures
subtitle: Prepared by A. G. Temple, F.S.A., Director of the Art Gallery of the Corporation of London
venue: Art Gallery of the Corporation of London (Guildhall Art Gallery)
label: Guildhall 1895
notes: This scan’s OCR drops most of the printed catalogue numbers: 71 have been restored from their sequence position, each flagged in its record’s note and corroborated by the catalogue’s Index of Artists. Three entries (nos. 71, 101, 133) have lost their headings in the scan — their artist and lender come from the catalogue’s own indexes and their titles are left empty; no. 116 prints no artist at all. Three sizes are illegible. Graves’s Century of Loan Exhibitions digests this exhibition and omits no work outright, but keys only 127 of its 138 numbers correctly, merging or misnumbering the rest — the printed catalogue is the authority here.

title: Catalogue of the Loan Collection of Pictures
subtitle: By Painters of the British School who have flourished during Her Majesty’s Reign
venue: Art Gallery of the Corporation of London (Guildhall Art Gallery)
label: Guildhall 1897
notes: This scan drops the printed margin numbers wholesale: 73 have been restored from their sequence position, each flagged in its record’s note and corroborated by the catalogue’s Index of Artists. Two sizes are illegible in the scan. Two unnumbered Jubilee exhibits shown with the exhibition — a marble bust and a miniature of Queen Victoria — stand outside the catalogue’s numbering and are not recorded here. Graves’s Century of Loan Exhibitions digests this exhibition but keys only 139 of its 167 works, folding several pictures into merged records and missing the lettered inserts — the printed catalogue is the authority here.

title: Catalogue of the Loan Collection of Pictures by Painters of the French School
subtitle: With Descriptive and Biographical Notes
venue: Art Gallery of the Corporation of London (Guildhall Art Gallery)
label: Guildhall 1898
notes: This copy of the catalogue is the pre-opening issue, marked “UNDER REVISION” on its cover; the records are taken from that text. 46 catalogue numbers have been restored from their sequence position, each flagged in its record’s note. Four sizes are incomplete in the scan. A separately numbered section of medals and objects of art (nos. 155–162) is not pictures and is not recorded here. Graves’s Century of Loan Exhibitions covers 143 of these 156 works in substance — the printed catalogue is the authority here.

title: Catalogue of the Loan Collection of Pictures and Drawings by J. M. W. Turner, R.A.
subtitle: And of a Selection of Pictures by some of his Contemporaries. With Descriptive and Biographical Notes
venue: Art Gallery of the Corporation of London (Guildhall Art Gallery)
label: Guildhall 1899
notes: Turner entries in Galleries I and II print no by-line; the artist is supplied from the catalogue’s title and flagged in each record. Gallery II prints no medium word — the works are the water colour drawings of its heading. Nos. 66–69 do not exist in the printed catalogue — the Liber Studiorum list passes from 65 to 70. 26 numbers have been restored from their sequence position, each flagged, and seven sizes are illegible in the scan. Graves’s Century of Loan Exhibitions keys only 119 of these 195 works, omitting the Liber Studiorum impressions and folding whole runs into unnumbered digests — the printed catalogue is the authority here.

title: Descriptive and Biographical Catalogue of the Exhibition of the Works of Spanish Painters
subtitle: By A. G. Temple, F.S.A., Director of the Art Gallery
venue: Art Gallery of the Corporation of London (Guildhall Art Gallery)
label: Guildhall 1901
notes: Gallery III is given over to Velasquez, with a life of the painter; Gallery IV opens with a life of Fortuny. This copy is the pre-opening issue, marked “Under revision” on its cover; the records stand as that text prints them. Three numbers have been restored from their sequence position, each flagged; no. 91 is entered under “Painter unknown”, as printed; seven entries at the end are etchings and lithographs entered by heading only, with no medium or size printed. Graves’s Century of Loan Exhibitions mixes this exhibition with another Guildhall show of 1901; he keys 197 of these 209 numbers and covers 200 in substance — the printed catalogue is the authority here.

title: Catalogue of the Exhibition of a Selection of Works by French and English Painters of the Eighteenth Century
subtitle: With Descriptive and Biographical Notes
venue: Art Gallery of the Corporation of London (Guildhall Art Gallery)
label: Guildhall 1902
notes: One number has been restored from its sequence position, flagged in its record; five sizes are not printed or are illegible in the scan, and six more are read with Graves’s corroboration, each flagged. Two entries are headed “French School” in place of a by-line, as printed. Graves’s Century of Loan Exhibitions keys 124 of these 153 numbers and covers 136 in substance, folding eleven Gainsboroughs into one digest record and missing all seven Lancrets — the printed catalogue is the authority here.

title: Catalogue of the Exhibition of a Selection of Works by Early and Modern Painters of the Dutch School. With Descriptive and Biographical Notes
subtitle: By A. G. Temple, F.S.A., Director of the Art Gallery
venue: Art Gallery of the Corporation of London (Guildhall Art Gallery)
label: Guildhall 1903
notes: The Twelfth Exhibition of the Guildhall series. Gallery I held the Gassiot bequest as part of the exhibition, but the catalogue prints no list of it, so those works are not recorded here. Eight catalogue numbers have been restored from their sequence position, each flagged in its record’s note. No. 100’s heading is lost in the scan — its artist and lender come from the catalogue’s own indexes, and its title, medium and size are not recorded. A printed notice in the catalogue records that nos. 137, 162 and 187 were returned to their owners in early June. Graves’s Century of Loan Exhibitions keys 144 of these 196 numbers and covers 158 in substance, lacking 38 outright — the printed catalogue is the authority here.

title: Catalogue of The Exhibition of Works by Irish Painters
subtitle: With Descriptive and Biographical Notes
venue: Art Gallery of the Corporation of London (Guildhall Art Gallery)
label: Guildhall 1904
notes: Catalogue no. 258 does not exist in the printed catalogue — a gap in the original numbering, not a lost record. 27 catalogue numbers were illegible in the scan and have been restored from their sequence position; each is flagged in its record’s note, shown under the title. Some entries print no size, medium or lender, and none has been inferred. The catalogue’s text carries ordinary OCR noise, so the odd title or name is garbled. No images in this first version.
